finding: CB-Score beta 0.2–1.0 met method-specific F1 and PR-AUC non-inferiority versus Full; beta 0.1 did not.
interpretation: Use beta 0.2 as strongest communication-preservation operating point; beta 0.4 as more conservative operating point.

finding: At beta 0.2, selected uplink fell by 82.8% and broadcast-equivalent E2E by 74.4%, with ΔF1=-0.0022 and ΔPR-AUC=-0.0002.
interpretation: Strongest central quantitative result, but not proof of selector superiority.
CB-Score cannot be presented as superior to Utility-Only, Utility/Cost, or Oort-style alternatives.
No general FPR-safety claim; use threshold-specific descriptive reporting.

finding: Full mean F1=0.0043, PR-AUC=0.1737 below test prevalence=0.2349, ROC-AUC=0.3491.
interpretation: Negative/generalization result; relative NI is operationally uninformative.

finding: CICIoT2023 performance degrades materially at alpha=0.1; CB F1=0.8267 versus 0.9214 at alpha=1.0.
interpretation: Selection does not eliminate severe non-IID sensitivity.

finding: Natural-source Full collapsed to FPR=1.0, while budgeted selectors achieved F1 0.8618–0.8905.
interpretation: Selection may regularize under domain skew, but this is descriptive and baseline failure must be discussed.

finding: On CICIoT2023, honest CB reduced malicious selection to about 5–10% under attack and preserved F1 better than Full, but forged utility raised malicious selection to about 70–91% and caused severe degradation.
interpretation: Robust to some honest-metadata attacks, vulnerable to metadata falsification; no Byzantine guarantee.

finding: No-Size had lower worst-case AUC than Raw/Noisy-Quantized; Raw and Noisy-Quantized retained near-perfect client-size leakage.
interpretation: Size metadata is a dominant leakage channel; minimization helps empirically but not formally.

finding: R4 ran on HP Pavilion i3-1215U CPU-only; execution order/cache effects make cross-method wall-clock comparisons unreliable.
interpretation: Report hardware and component overhead only; do not use wall-clock speedup as a central claim.
